articles.title: Trump says will meet North Korea’s Kim later this year
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and then-US President Donald Trump held a historic meeting at the Military Demarcation Line. Trump briefly stepped into North Korea, becoming the first sitting US president to do so. This significant diplomatic event aimed to foster dialogue on denuclearization and regional peace, highlighting complex international relations.

articles.title: Controversial Superhero Series Has Become a Smash Hit on Streaming Despite Backlash
articles.summary: The new DCU series 'Lanterns' has achieved significant early streaming success, topping HBO Max's U.S. TV rankings despite initial controversy. Its rapid ascent places it ahead of other popular shows, demonstrating strong viewer engagement. This success highlights the evolving landscape of digital entertainment platforms and the audience's continued interest in superhero franchises, crucial for understanding contemporary media consumption trends.

articles.title: Lowes Foods Weekly Ad: 8/19-8/25
articles.summary: Lowes Foods is running weekly ad deals until August 25, featuring discounts on popular brands like Pepsi and Clorox. Shoppers can find Buy One Get One offers on items such as sweet blueberries and other groceries at their local stores. These promotions focus on consumer goods and household essentials, reflecting current domestic retail trends and consumer spending opportunities within the nation.

articles.title: Ram Charan Not in Irumudi: Mallepoola Pallaki Cameo Rumours Clarified
articles.summary: Actor Ram Charan will not appear in the 'Mallepoola Pallaki' song from the upcoming film 'Irumudi', officially denying earlier rumours of a cameo. This news might disappoint fans who anticipated his presence. The film, starring Ravi Teja, is scheduled for release in theatres on August 21st, proceeding without Charan's rumoured involvement, a clarification important for industry followers.

articles.title: No death during NEET paper leak agitation but many killed in protests under Congress rule: Kiren Rijiju
articles.summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju asserted that no lives were lost during recent student protests concerning NEET paper leaks. He critically contrasted this, claiming numerous individuals were killed due to police firing during past Congress government tenures. Rijiju's statement highlights the government's handling of the protests while drawing a historical comparison to previous administrations regarding law and order and protest management.
